section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section presents findings from a single study (Study X) examining the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) among Malaysian women in Kuala Lumpur. The study found a two-factor structure of the BAS (General Body Appreciation and Body Image Investment) in this non-Western setting, contrasting with the unidimensional structure found in Western samples, and revealed that General Body Appreciation was significantly negatively correlated with participants' BMI. The authors recommend caution in using the BAS across different cultural groups and suggest that the scale's structure and interpretation may differ across cultures.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) among Malaysian women in Kuala Lumpur. The study found a two-factor structure (General Body Appreciation and Body Image Investment) rather than the unidimensional structure found in Western samples, suggesting cross-cultural differences in body image attitudes. The study also found that General Body Appreciation was significantly negatively correlated with BMI, consistent with previous research in German-speaking samples.
